summary: Lexington County tower built around 1936; the SC Forestry Commission still owns it, and a nearby keeper's house is a part-time sheriff's substation.

events.note: Built around 1936 per the register; Wikipedia gives 1936 as the first build year
SC Forestry Commission closed its tower system on 1 October 1993; the register says this tower is still SCFC-owned

evidence.supports: built around 1936, 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 with 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: Built around 1936, this 100' Aermotor LS-40 tower with 7'x7' cab

evidence.supports: one of three still owned by SCFC in Lexington County
evidence.quote: is one of three still owned by the SC Forestry Commission in Lexington county

evidence.supports: keeper's house used part time as sheriff's substation
evidence.quote: A nearby keeper's house is currently used part time as a law enforcement substation for the Lexington County Sheriff's Department
The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: first tower erected August 1930 near Camden
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.
a fire lookout tower first built in 1936

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the tower is 499 feet tall; the register gives an elevation of 499 ft (152 m) and a height of 100 ft for the tower itself, so the Wikipedia figure probably mixes up the elevation with the tower's height.

notes_for_editor: Only the register, the SCFC history page and Wikipedia were readable. WLTX and Post and Courier articles on the tower returned 403 and 429 and were not used; they would likely add access and staffing detail. Access and staffing are left out because no readable source states them. The Wikipedia article cites the register, so its 1936 date is not independent. A search snippet from an SCFC 'important fires' page mentions a different 'Gaston Fire' (a wildfire elsewhere, not linked to this tower); the page was not read and it should not be tied to the tower without a source.
